prompt_text: I need a new air conditioner installed in Atlanta. Which specific HVAC companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
I can recommend a short list of specific companies to call in the Atlanta area, plus exactly why to call them and what to ask. If you want, give me your ZIP code and I’ll tailor the list to businesses that serve your neighborhood.

Recommended companies to call
- Coolray & Mr. Plumber (Coolray)
  - Why: Large regional company with a big Atlanta presence, offers same-day installs/repairs, financing, and carries a range of brands. Good for fast service and multiple system options.
- Service Experts Heating & Air Conditioning (Atlanta franchise)
  - Why: National franchise with local technicians, NATE-certified techs, comprehensive install warranties and maintenance plans. Good for consistent process and longer-term service plans.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter (Heating & Air)
  - Why: Large multi-service company with 24/7 emergency service and many local technicians. Helpful if you want emergency availability plus planned installation.
- One Hour Heating & Air / Benjamin Franklin (local franchise)
  - Why: Franchise model emphasizes on-time service windows and satisfaction guarantees; they provide installs, maintenance plans and financing options.
- A reputable independent local contractor (how to find one)
  - Why: Many independent Atlanta HVAC contractors offer lower prices, more personalized service, and installers who specialize in energy-efficient installs. You’ll need to vet them carefully, but they often deliver very good value and workmanship.

Why I’m suggesting a mix
- National/regional brands (Service Experts, ARS, One Hour, Coolray) give consistent processes, financing, extended warranties and often 24/7 service.
- Independent/local contractors can be more flexible on pricing and may give more personalized attention — but you must check references and credentials.

What to ask every company when you call
- Are you licensed and insured in Georgia? (Ask for license number and insurance proof.)
- Will you perform a Manual J load calculation for proper sizing? (Don’t accept a “rule of thumb” size.)
- Which brands and SEER ratings do you install and recommend for Atlanta’s climate?
- Can you provide a written, itemized estimate (equipment, labor, permits, disposal)?
- What are the labor and compressor/parts warranties? Is a separate labor warranty available?
- Do you offer financing or rebates? Will you pull permits and arrange inspections?
- Who does the install (company crews or subcontractors)? Are techs NATE-certified?
- Do you offer a maintenance plan and after-install service response times?

How to choose between estimates
- Make sure each bid uses the same assumptions (Manual J load, same efficiency/brand, same scope).
- Compare total installed cost, warranty terms, and included items (thermostat, refrigerant charge, duct work).
- Check online reviews (Google, Yelp), BBB rating, and ask for local references.
- Prefer bids that include permitting, disposal of old equipment, and a clear performance guarantee.

If you want, I can:
- Find 3–5 specific installers that serve your exact Atlanta ZIP code and provide phone numbers and recent reviews.
- Review quotes you receive and point out red flags and which offer best value.

Tell me your ZIP code or paste any quotes you already have and I’ll help next.
